sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion at this exact site
sites.functional_impact_measured: Flow cytometry with fluorescent anti-FLAG antibodies confirmed cell-surface display; MMP-dependent cleavage of the ectodomain (including the FLAG tag) was detected as a decrease in FLAG fluorescence, demonstrating the construct is functional for MMP-mediated shedding.
sites.rationale: L2 explicitly names R489 and G490 as the flanking residues of the 3×FLAG insertion in full-length, membrane-anchored DAG1. Python confirms seq[488]='R' and seq[489]='G', matching the paper exactly. Position 489 is deep within the extracellular domain (30–752), 264 residues from the TM boundary, satisfying all distance constraints. The construct was detected on the cell surface and used in a functional MMP-cleavage assay, providing the highest validation level. Full-length DAG1 construct with 3×FLAG inserted between R489 and G490; expressed in cells and detected on the cell surface by fluorescently-labeled anti-FLAG antibodies via flow cytometry. Loss of FLAG signal upon MMP cleavage was used as a functional readout of ectodomain shedding.

sources.claim: In the event of MMP cleavage, the Flag tag (inserted between amino acids R489 and G490) would be cleaved off with the majority of the dystroglycan ectodomain, decreasing binding by fluorescently-labeled anti-Flag antibodies, and therefore, fluorescence as readout by flow cytometry ( Figure S6 , S7 left).

sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion at this exact site
sites.functional_impact_measured: Flow cytometry with fluorescent anti-HA antibodies confirmed cell-surface display of the HA-tagged construct; the tag persisted after MMP cleavage of the distal ectodomain, confirming surface retention and trafficking. No independent functional assay (e.g., ligand binding) was reported.
sites.rationale: L3 explicitly names P724 and R725 as the flanking residues of the HA insertion in full-length, membrane-anchored DAG1. Python confirms seq[723]='P' and seq[724]='R', matching the paper exactly. Position 724 is extracellular (30–752), 29 residues from the TM start at 753, well above the >=3 residue minimum. The construct traffics to the cell surface and the tag is accessible to antibodies, but no ligand-binding or signalling assay was reported. Full-length DAG1 construct with HA tag inserted between P724 and R725; expressed in cells and detected on the cell surface by fluorescently-labeled anti-HA antibodies via flow cytometry. This site is in the membrane-proximal ectodomain region retained after MMP cleavage, used as a marker of total surface DAG1 expression.

sources.claim: However, the HA epitope tag (between amino acids P724 and R725) is found on the small part of the dystroglycan ectodomain that is retained even after MMP cleavage, allowing it to act as a marker of overall cell surface dystroglycan expression by binding to fluorescently labeled anti-HA antibodies ( Figure S6 right).

sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion in the same loop or domain
sites.functional_impact_measured: FLAG-tagged construct was expressed and used for purification and detection of secreted/expressed αDG, confirming successful folding and trafficking. No cell-surface flow cytometry or functional ligand-binding assay was explicitly reported in the cited clip.
sites.rationale: L4 states the FLAG tag was placed 'at the N-terminus of the αDG cDNA after the signal peptide,' which maps to insert_after_residue=29 (the last SP residue, S29) in UniProt canonical numbering. Python confirms seq[28]='S' and seq[29]='H'. The mature N-terminus (residue 30) is extracellular, so the tag is on the extracellular face and will not be cleaved with the signal peptide. Ranked third because the cited clip does not report explicit cell-surface detection by flow cytometry or a functional assay. Full-length DAG1 αDG cDNA construct with FLAG tag placed at the N-terminus after the signal peptide (after residue 29, the last SP residue); used to enrich for full-length protein and enable purification and detection of expressed αDG.

sources.claim: Because we wanted to enrich for full-length protein, we also placed a FLAG epitope tag at the N-terminus of the cDNA after the signal peptide.

literature_notes: All four ledger lines were evaluated. L1 and L2 both describe the same 3×FLAG insertion at R489|G490 in full-length DAG1; L2 was chosen as the primary supporting clip because it explicitly names both flanking residues (R489, G490), satisfying the 'validated' position_evidence criterion. L1 corroborates the same site and also mentions the HA site at 724|725 (covered by L3). L4 describes a FLAG tag after the signal peptide on the αDG N-terminus; the clip does not specify a residue number but the topology landmark (signal peptide 1–29, mature N-terminus 30) uniquely determines insert_after_residue=29. No intracellular or function-abrogating insertions were reported in the ledger for DAG1.
